notes_list.title: E/Z Configuration
notes_list.basic_overview: E/Z nomenclature describes alkene geometry when each alkene carbon has two different substituents.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Apply CIP independently on each alkene carbon. If higher-priority groups are on the same side → Z; opposite sides → E.
notes_list.examples: 2-butene has E and Z stereoisomers. Substituted alkenes can have E/Z even when cis/trans terminology is ambiguous.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Alkene geometry can be preserved or changed depending on the mechanism. Syn additions can be stereospecific; carbocation intermediates can reduce stereospecificity.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: 1. Identify two substituents on each sp2 carbon. 2. Assign CIP priorities. 3. Compare spatial side of high-priority groups.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: E/Z is configurational; rotation around C=C is not free under ordinary conditions because π bonding must be disrupted.
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Important for addition, elimination and stereospecific reaction questions.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not equate E with “trans” universally; trans/cis requires a comparable pair of groups.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
